speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth for each year in the past five years (a) in how many and what percentage of cases have the 80:20 fund-raising rule requiring at least 80% of funds raised for foreign charitable purposes be applied towards local charitable purposes been waived for fund-raising activities; (b) of the cases where this 80:20 rule is waived, what are the top three target donor groups and beneficiaries; and (c) when will the Ministry next review this 80:20 rule.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: So, I also kindly ask him to refer to our reply given then, as it remains relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: More recently, waivers were also granted for appeals supporting relief efforts for the Türkiye–Syria Earthquake.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should also thank him for meeting up with the non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to discuss this issue and the concerns they have about raising funds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I think he would also have heard about how difficult it has been for them to get this waiver.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For one, I am going to ask whether the Government can be more prescriptive and lay out what are the specific safeguards that are needed in place to mitigate the risks in terms of foreign fund-raising.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And second, could I ask when is the next review of the Charities regulations?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Just to take a step back – the intent of the 80:20 rule is to ensure that these funds that are raised from the public are used primarily to benefit locals and also local causes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: A concession is made where a proportion of the funds – in this case, 20% – is allowed to flow overseas for charitable purposes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Because it is important o ensure: one, the accountability and transparency of permit holders since public funds are involved; and two, that the external flow of funds for overseas causes to foreign entities are legitimate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: All organisations have to apply for a foreign fund-raising permit from the COC if there is a need to raise funds for a foreign charitable purpose, and to seek waiver of the 80:20 rule where appropriate or when required.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In the case of smaller organisations like some of the NGOs that we met, who may not have enough resources to monitor its partners and affiliates, these organisations may consider partnering with those who are equipped to do so and who already have valid fund-raising permits in place.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The COC will continue to review the 80:20 policy and will update the Member in due time.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We can and have already been, on a case-by-case basis, waiving the rule, as I mentioned in my reply to the PQ and supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We thank the Member for his continued support for organisations who are working hard to support worthwhile causes overseas and, also, to Singaporeans and Singapore residents who have contributed to these causes.
